bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang: Memory Shortage to Last 'Several More Years'; Massive Demand Across Entire Supply Chain
bullets.body: Jensen Huang stated at GTC Korea that 'demand is enormous' across the full supply chain from wafers to silicon photonics to cable connectors. He separately told attendees that the memory shortage will persist for 'quite a few years,' a direct bullish signal for HBM/DRAM suppliers. Huang also answered 'yes' when asked if it's time to buy Nvidia stock.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Huang to Meet Samsung Vice Chairman Monday; SK Cooperation Plan Also Due
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is scheduled to meet Samsung's Vice Chairman and separately reveal a cooperation plan with SK Chairman Chey on Monday. Multiple high-level meetings signal deepening relationships with South Korean chip and memory partners.

bullets.title: MRVL Added to S&P 500 Effective June 22, Replacing Pool Corp
bullets.body: Marvell Technology ($MRVL) and Flex ($FLEX) announced as new S&P 500 additions, effective before market open June 22. Pool Corp and Campbell's are being replaced. Index inclusion will drive passive buying flows into MRVL.

bullets.title: Apple WWDC Monday: Dan Ives Expects 'Fireworks' on AI; Crisis Meeting Context
bullets.body: Apple is hosting WWDC with a Tim Cook keynote Monday at 1PM ET, with multiple analysts expecting major AI announcements including a new AI-powered Siri. Context: AAPL reportedly held an internal crisis meeting in early 2025 over failed Apple Intelligence and delayed Siri, with rivals OpenAI, Google, and Meta advancing. Dan Ives uses 'Fireworks' language to describe expectations.

bullets.title: Meta Weighs Tens of Billions in New Stock Offering; Stock Down 7%
bullets.body: Meta is reportedly weighing raising tens of billions via a new share sale to fund AI capex, per the FT, following Google's $80B equity raise. The report triggered a 6-7% intraday decline in META shares. Separately, Meta is exploring a $200/month consumer AI agent subscription tier.

bullets.title: Google Signs $920M/Month SpaceX Cloud Deal; $30B Total for ~110k NVIDIA GPUs
bullets.body: SpaceX's amended S-1 disclosed a cloud services agreement with Google at $920M/month from October 2026 through June 2029, involving approximately 110,000 NVIDIA GPUs, CPUs, and memory. Google retains ownership of AI models. SpaceX can terminate if GPU delivery by September is missed. This confirms ongoing massive Blackwell GPU demand.

bullets.title: Broader Mag-7 Equity Fundraising Wave: Up to $600B Possible Over 12 Months
bullets.body: Fintwit estimates Meta, Google, Anthropic, SpaceX, and OpenAI could raise $350-400B from public markets in 9-12 months, with Amazon and Microsoft potentially joining to push totals to $550-600B. Observers note debt markets have effectively closed for these issuers, forcing expensive equity sales to fund $5T in aggregate capex.

bullets.title: Market Selloff Friday: Nasdaq-100 Drops 4.8%, S&P -2.6%; VIX Surges 36%
bullets.body: Friday saw the S&P 500 fall 2.6% (worst day since October) and the Nasdaq-100 sink 4.8% — reportedly the largest daily point decline in Nasdaq history. The catalyst was a blowout May jobs report (+172K vs +88K expected) that reignited Fed rate-hike expectations. VIX surged 36% and dealer gamma turned negative. S&P 500 put volume hit an all-time high.

bullets.title: Strong May Jobs Report (+172K vs +88K): Inflation and Rate Focus Ahead of CPI
bullets.body: May payrolls blew out estimates by 84K, with the 3-month average hitting 188K (highest since March 2024). BofA's Hartnett warns of elevated June event risk and a CPI print that 'could pop the bubble.' Fed futures moved to price an 85% chance of a rate hike this year. Kevin Hassett (NEC) signaled White House appetite for cuts, raising concerns about new Fed chair Warsh's independence.

bullets.title: Trade Desk COO Exits After Just 7 Months; Hired From Google
bullets.body: The Trade Desk's COO (Anders) departed after only 7 months in the role, having been recruited from a 13-year tenure at Google. Fintwit commentary suggests potential leadership friction or strategic misalignment.

bullets.title: Broadcom Enters Bear Market, Down 20%+ From Wednesday ATH; VCSEL Strategy Questioned
bullets.body: AVGO entered bear market territory by Friday's close, having shed more than 20% from its Wednesday all-time high. Separately, a semiconductor analyst questioned why AVGO is attempting a 3.2T NPO VCSEL solution despite prior VCSEL failures.

bullets.title: NVDA Silicon Photonics Architecture Debate: CPO vs. NPO for Rubin Ultra
bullets.body: Fintwit semiconductor analysts are debating whether NVDA will use CPO (as in Spectrum X) or NPO for Rubin Ultra's inter-rack optical interconnects. An unverified 'conspiracy theory' circulated that Kyber mid-plane PCBs have yield issues and CPO is not ready, with NPO proposed as an alternative. AVGO's VCSEL approach also under scrutiny.

bullets.title: Intel Foundry Utilization Concern: 70-80% of Tiles May Remain Unallocated
bullets.body: A semiconductor analyst tracking Intel foundry noted that 70-80% (or more) of tiles remain unallocated. Intel's wafer volume with TSMC in 2025-26 is being tracked as a key demand signal. Questions raised about whether Intel's fab52 economics can compete if Nova products are more cost-effective at TSMC.

bullets.title: Corning / TSMC / ASE: Glass Substrate CPO Gaining Traction for 2028-29 Volume Production
bullets.body: Corning is demonstrating large-format glass substrates for chip-to-chip optical interconnects (CPO), with TSMC evaluating for CoPoS panel packaging and ASE qualifying glass. LPKF (Germany) claims a moat via hafnium high-k patents and LIDE technology; Samsung lost a court case forcing use of SK Trichem (LPKF JV). Volume production expected 2028-29. Intel and Samsung are named as adopters.

bullets.title: Memory Shortage Multi-Year Outlook Boosts MU; Jensen Huang Cites AI Demand
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts highlight Jensen Huang's explicit memory shortage forecast lasting 'several more years' as a direct catalyst for MU and broader memory names. One trader notes MU PE at 10 with implied volatility at 300%. Separately, MU is identified as preferred over DRAM ETF for higher volatility/upside potential.

bullets.title: AAOI: $600M ATM for Laser Fab Capacity; Vertical Integration Patent Filed
bullets.body: AAOI is planning a $600M ATM to build laser fab capacity, with $471M/month revenue expected H1 2027 at lower market cap ranges. Author frames dilution as accretive. Separately, AAOI filed a patent related to vertical integration.

bullets.title: USD/JPY Above 160: Japan MoF Intervention Risk Flagged for Next Week
bullets.body: USD/JPY crossed back above 160, the level at which the Japanese Ministry of Finance previously dumped $30B in a single intervention. Multiple fintwit accounts flagging elevated risk of MoF action next week.

bullets.title: Iran-US Tensions: Hormuz Toll (~$1.5-2M/Ship), US Shoots Down Drones; Deal 'Very Close'
bullets.body: Iran is charging $1.5-2M per ship transiting Hormuz, and the US shot down Iranian drones near the strait. Trump told NBC an Iran deal is 'very close' with only two minor sticking points, while separately threatening military destruction if no deal is reached. Iran's parliament speaker threatened 'painful' responses to Israeli strikes. Markets appear to be pricing in a deal, per fintwit commentary.

bullets.title: MSFT Named as Clear Enterprise AI Leader by Former OpenAI Employee
bullets.body: A former OpenAI employee stated Microsoft is 'the clear leader in enterprise AI,' with an advantage that Amazon and Nvidia would find difficult to close. Separately, MSFT is the sole Mag-7 name said to remain cash flow positive amid broad peer spending.

bullets.title: EQIX Holding Well Amid Selloff; Large Fundamental Buyers Added in Q1
bullets.body: Equinix was flagged as an outperformer during Friday's broad selloff, with noted large fundamental investors having added EQIX in size in the prior quarter.
